 SCCH.13 3 MVC.6074/2023  JUDGMENT This petition under Section 166 Motor Vehicles Act 1989 is filed seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the death of Sri. Yarappa S/o Late Thimmarayappa, in a road traffic accident.
2. It is the specific case of the petitioner that on 21-07-2022 at about 11:00 p.m., Yarappa was standing in front of Santosh Bar behind Maluru Bus Stand, Karachi Extension, Maluru Town, Kolar.

At that time, the driver of the Maruti Swift Dzire car bearing registration number KA-08-M-2717,
hereinafter called the offending vehicle, drove the same at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against Yarappa. Due to the tremendous impact, Yarappa sustained severe injuries all over the body.
Immediately, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Maluru.
After first aid, he was shifted to SNR Hospital, Kolar, wherein he was treated as an inpatient from 21- 07-2022 to 24-07-2022, and on 24-07-2022 he succumbed to the fatal injuries.
After post-mortem, the dead body was handed over to the petitioners and they performed his last rites.
3. At the time of accident, deceased was 70 years old and working as a agriculturist and also working as a coolie and was earning Rs.15,000/- p.m.
The deceased contributing his entire income to his family.
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife, Petitioners No.2 and 3 are children of the deceased and due to untimely death of deceased, they have suffered mental shock and agony and financial loss.
It is requested to award Rs.50,00,000/- compensation with interest from the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the insurer and insured of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.1 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Respondent No.2 did not turn up and was accordingly placed exparte.
5. Respondent No. 1 has filed its written statement and admitted the issuance of the policy but contended that its liability is subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
It has denied the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.
It is further contended that, as per the complaint and FIR, the accident was caused by an unknown vehicle, and the offending vehicle was implicated after a lapse of four days from the accident.

It is also contended that, as per the complaint, the deceased was a beggar; therefore, the petitioners are not the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased and are not entitled to compensation.
6. Respondent No. 1 has also contended that the owner of the offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied with the provisions of Section 134( c) and Section 158(6) of the MV Act.
It is further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having a valid driving licence.

The respondent has denied that the accident was caused due to the negligence of the driver of the offending car and, on the other hand, asserted that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the deceased.
It has further denied the age, avocation, and income of the deceased, as well as the relationship and dependency of the petitioners, and prayed for dismissal of the petition.

7. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :-
1.

Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Yarappa died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 21-07- 2022 at about 11.00 p.m. behind Malur Bus stand, opp.Santhosh Bar, Karanji Extension Malur town, Kolar, due to the rash or negligence driving of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-08-M-2717 by its driver ?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
if so, what amount and from whom?
4 . What order or award ?
8. In support of their claim, Petitioner No.1/wife of deceased is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.14.
On the other hand Respondent No.1 has not chosen to adduce any oral evidence.
9. I heard the counsel on both sides and have perused the material on record.

10. By considering the evidence and materials available on record and after hearing the arguments my findings to the above issues are as under:

Issue No.4 : As per the final order, for the following:
REASON 11. ISSUE NO.1 PW1 deposed that on 21-07- 2022 at about 11:00 p.m., Yarappa was standing in front of Santosh Bar behind Maluru Bus Stand, Karachi Extension, Maluru Town, Kolar.

At that time, the driver of the Maruti Swift Dzire car bearing registration number KA-08-M-2717,
hereinafter called the offending vehicle, drove the same at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against Yarappa.
Due to the tremendous impact, Yarappa sustained severe injuries all over the body.
Immediately, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Maluru.
After first aid, he was shifted to SNR Hospital, Kolar, wherein he was treated as an inpatient from 21- 07-2022 to 24-07-2022, and on 24-07-2022 he succumbed to the fatal injuries.

12. In order to substantiate their case, the petitioners have produced the FIR, complaint, charge sheet, spot mahazar, wound sketch, IMV report, post- mortem report, and inquest report at Exhibit P-1 to P- 6.

The contention of Respondent No. 1 is that the offending vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and that the petitioners, in active collusion with the police, created false documents in order to implicate the vehicle and claim compensation.
13. During the course of cross-examination of PW1

, it was suggested that at the time of the accident,
the deceased had consumed alcohol and, in a drunken state, fell into a drainage.
It was further suggested that, in order to suppress this fact, a complaint was lodged after a delay of four days.
PW1 denied the said suggestion.
She admits that she came to know about the death of her husband only three days after the incident.

14. Respondent No. 1 contends that the complainant, Manjunath, a resident of the deceased's village, himself lodged the complaint stating that the deceased was a beggar, and that the accident was caused by an unknown vehicle.
It is further contended that only after four days the offending vehicle was falsely implicated in order to claim compensation.
15. There is no contra evidence placed on record by Respondent No. 1 to prove that the accident was not caused by the offending car but by some other vehicle.
Except for suggestions and bare contentions, no single document has been produced by Respondent No. 1.
On the contrary, the evidence of PW1 stands corroborated by the contemporaneous police documents produced at Exhibit P-1 to P-6.
In the present case, no independent witnesses have been examined nor any cogent material placed on record to support the plea of collusion.

If indeed collusion existed,
Respondent No. 1 ought to have initiated appropriate proceedings before the investigating authority or competent court, which has not been done.
16. Mere allegations unsupported by proof cannot be accepted.

In motor accident claim cases, the standard of proof is not proof beyond reasonable doubt but the touchstone of preponderance of Lalithamma vs Go Digit General Insurance Limited on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17203777/
4 probabilities.

sentences.text: Applying this principle, the case of the petitioners stands fortified by both oral and documentary evidence, while the defence of Respondent No. 1 remains unsubstantiated.

Accordingly, I hold that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car,
resulting in the death of Yarappa.
Hence I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:

Here, the controversy is confined to whether the petitioners are the legal heirs of the deceased Yarappa notwithstanding the FIR's description of the victim as a "beggar." PW-1 (petitioner No.1) has deposed that she is the wife of the deceased and that petitioners Nos.2 and 3 are his daughters.
To establish this, she has produced Aadhaar cards, the family tree, and the death certificate, marked as Exs.P-7 to P-14.

The death certificate is a public document and an entry in an official register made by a public servant in the discharge of his duties; it therefore attracts the presumption of correctness under Section 35 of the Evidence Act, and its regularity is supported by the presumption under Section 114, Illustration (e).
The family tree certificate carries evidentiary value as a contemporaneous record of relationships.
The Aadhaar cards, although not conclusive proof of marital status by themselves, corroborate identity, address and family linkage when read with the public records.
This documentary set is further supported by the inquest, which records that the dead body was released to the petitioners an administrative act consistent only with their status as next of kin.

Significantly, none of these documents has been impeached through any cogent cross-examination of the issuing authorities or by producing superior or contradictory records such as a rival family tree, marriage register entries disproving the marriage, or any succession proceedings excluding the petitioners.
18. Against this, Respondent No.1 places sole reliance on the FIR/complaint recital that the victim was a "beggar," and urges that the petitioners are neither legal heirs nor dependents.
This contention cannot prevail for multiple reasons.

First, the FIR is not a conclusive instrument on civil status; it is a contemporaneous account of the occurrence, often based on the informant's limited knowledge and intended to set the criminal law in motion--not to adjudicate matrimonial or filial relationships.
A stray descriptor like "beggar" neither disproves a subsisting marriage nor negates paternity.
Secondly, even on facts, PW-1's cross-examination only shows that the deceased had suffered a left-leg amputation about a decade earlier.
Physical disability or unemployment does not translate into abandonment of family or severance of legal relationships.

PW-1 specifically denied the suggestions that the deceased had no family, that she had deserted him, or that no one was looking after him; these suggestions remain mere suggestions--no independent witness (such as the complainant Manjunath) was examined, no investigating officer was summoned, and no documentary proof of desertion or alternative next-of- kin was produced.
Thirdly, in claim proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act, issues of relationship and entitlement are determined on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
The petitioners' case is supported by public documents (Exs. P-7 to P-14) and by the inquest handing-over; the respondent's case is supported only by an FIR epithet and unproved insinuations.
On this balance, the evidentiary scale tilts decisively in favour of the petitioners.
Finally and in law even if the deceased had been indigent, that circumstance is irrelevant to heirship.

Spouses and children are "legal representatives" within the meaning of the Act and are entitled to maintain the claim; financial dependency bears on Lalithamma vs Go Digit General Insurance Limited on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17203777/
5 quantification under the "loss of dependency" head, not on locus to claim.

sentences.text:
19. For these reasons, the Court finds that the petitioners have satisfactorily proved, through Exs.
P-7 to P-14 and unshaken testimony of PW-1, that petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioners Nos.2 and 3 are the daughters of the deceased Yarappa.
There is no contra material produced by Respondent no 1 to dislodge this proof.
The plea that the deceased was a beggar is, best an unsubstantiated assertion and does not defeat the petitioners' status as legal heirs.
The petitioners are the legal heirs of the deceased.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
20. Issue No.3: I have already discussed under Issue No. 2 that the deceased Erappa left behind his wife (petitioner No.1) and two daughters (petitioners Nos.2 and 3), who are his legal heirs.

Hence,
the petitioners are entitled to claim compensation as legal representatives.

The respondent No.1 has relied upon a decision reported in MFA No.8452/2019 -Smt.Jabeena Taj Vs. The Head Master and others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka observed that the deceased was striving hard for her survival living separately from the family near the mosque and was depending on the amount collected from the begging.

entities.text: Jabeena Taj Vs. The Head Master and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the said decision is distinguishable on facts.
In that case, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka observed that since the claimants have failed to establish their dependency upon the deceased.
However, the present case stands on a different footing.
Here the petitioners have produced cogent evidence all of which clearly establish the relationship of the deceased with the petitioners.
Mere mentioning in the FIR and complaint that an unknown person or begger was invoked cannot override the substantial evidence produced by the petitioners.
The plea of the respondent No.1 that deceased was a begger remains unproved.
Therefore, the citation relied by the respondent No.1 is not applicable to the case on hand.

21. Coming to the question of income, the petitioners have specifically pleaded that the deceased was aged about 70 years at the time of the accident and was working as an agriculturist as well as a coolie, earning Rs.15,000 per month, and that he was contributing his entire earnings to the family.
It is true that no independent documentary proof, such as land records or wage slips, has been produced to substantiate his exact occupation and monthly income.

However, in motor accident claim cases, it is a settled principle that the tribunal should take a realistic and pragmatic view rather than insist on strict proof, particularly when the deceased was engaged in informal or unorganized sector employment where documentary evidence is seldom available.

22. In this regard, guidance may be drawn from the notional income chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which prescribes notional income for different years to be applied in motor accident claims where there is no documentary proof.
For the year 2020, the prescribed notional income is Rs.15,500/- per month.
The petitioner has claimed the income of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- per month, which is in fact slightly less than the notional income fixed by KSLSA for that year.
Hence, the income claimed by the petitioner appears reasonable and in consonance with the notional yardstick.
23. Accordingly, for the purpose of computing compensation, the income of the deceased is taken at Rs.15,000/- per month.
This figure is consistent with both the petitioners' pleadings and the KSLSA notional income chart, and is also a just and fair basis to assess the dependency loss.

sentences.text: The PW-1 has produced Ex.P.10- Aadhaar card of deceased, which shows the year of birth of deceased as 1948 and considering the same, he was aged 74 years as on the date of accident and proper multiplier applicable to the case is 5.
As the age of the deceased is 74 years, no future prospects is to be added.

As there are 3 dependents, 1/3rd of the income is to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses and the annual income would come to (Rs.10,000 X 12)
Rs.1,20,000/- and applying 5 multiplier
, Petitioners are awarded Rs.6,00,000/- towards loss of dependency.
25. CONSORTIUM:

By following the guidelines of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs- Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others., this Tribunal deems it proper to hold that the Petitioners are entitled .44,000/- each under the head of consortium as Petitioner No.1 has lost her husband, Petitioner No.2 and 3 have lost their father.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs- Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 26. Loss to estate:
It appears that the Petitioner No.1 has lost her husband and the daughters have lost their father.
Hence, .20,000/- is awarded towards loss to estate.
27. Funeral Expenses:
Petitioners have claimed that they have spent .1,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral & obsequies ceremony expenses.
By considering the facts and circumstances it would be proper to award .16,500/- for the funeral and other incidental expenses.

28. In all, the amount of compensation awarded by this Tribunal to the Petitioners under various headings is as follows :
Sl.No Nature of Compensation Amount 1. Loss of dependency Rs. 6,00,000/-
2. Loss of consortium Rs. 1,32,000/-
to Petitioners 3. Loss to estate Rs. 20,000/-
4. Transportation of Rs. 16,500/-
dead body, Funeral & obsequies Expenses Total Rs. 7,68,500/-
29.
Liability:
The Petitioners have lead cogent evidence and have proved that the accident was occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle.
The policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the insurer and insured of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
However, in view of the issuance policy, the Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioners with interest at 6% per annum.
With these observations, I have answered Issue No.3 partly in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition
filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioners are awarded compensation of .7,68,500/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the realization.
Respondent No.1 shall deposit the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of amount, an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- is apportioned to the petitioner No.1.
Out of remaining amount equal amount is apportioned to petitioner No.2 and 3.
After deposit of amount, entire amount with interest in respect of petitioner No.1 to 3 shall be disbursed to them through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Draw award accordingly.
